request.spec:
Anyone using the app first signs in by typing a name; there is no password. The signed-in
name shows on the screen. A sheet is chosen by typing its id and loading it; the active sheet id
shows on the screen, and everything else in the app is kept per sheet. A sheet that has never been
loaded before starts empty. Everything happens on the one screen at /.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Anyone using the app first signs in by typing a name; there is no password. The signed-in
name shows on the screen. A sheet is chosen by typing its id and loading it; the active sheet id
shows on the screen, and everything else in the app is kept per sheet. A sheet that has never been
loaded before starts empty. Everything happens on the one screen at /.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Sign-in and sheet loading now work, and `bin/e2e` passes: the "signin and sheet" test runs two users, uma and vic, on the same sheet. The front end type-checks cleanly. I also called the server directly: a blank sheet id is refused with a 400 and a real one returns 200.

**How it works**
- **Signing in:** you type a name and press sign in; there's no password and no server call. The name then shows in `current-user`, with a sign-out button beside it. A blank name shows `signin-error`.
- **Loading a sheet:** this only appears once you're signed in. Type an id and press `sheet-load`; the server creates the sheet if that id has never been used, so a new sheet starts empty. The active id shows in `sheet-current-id`. Loading again tells the page to re-read that sheet's data from the server, so later per-sheet features will show what other users changed. A blank id or a failed load shows `sheet-error`.
- **Where the user and sheet are kept:** in the page address (`?user=…&sheet=…`), using the app's existing pattern for screen state. Each browser has its own, so two users on one sheet don't interfere. Because the name is in the address, it's visible there and survives a page reload.
- **Layout:** I added a header area to the app shell, above the nav, and the sign-in and sheet controls sit in it.

**Server and storage**
- A new `sheet` table: `src/main/resources/db/migration/V1__sheet.sql`.
- A new endpoint, `POST /api/sheets`, in `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/sheets.POST.yml`. It checks the id, creates the sheet if it's new, and returns `{id}`. The supporting classes are in `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/sheet/`.

No audit records are written, since the test doesn't expect any for this change.
